filesystem-rw.description: Read-write access to source code, specs and skills. Agents can create and edit files here during development.
filesystem-rw.justification: Minimum scope: only folders where agents actively generate or modify artifacts. Excludes docs and data (business sources) to prevent unintended writes.

filesystem-readonly.description: Read-only access to NovaTech business documentation and RAG retrieval corpus. Agents can read but must not modify these sources.
filesystem-readonly.justification: Business sources must be immutable from agent perspective: docs/novatech contains the authoritative NovaTech documents (Annex A); data/retrieval-corpus contains the indexed chunks (Annex B). Any modification would corrupt the knowledge base and violate ADR-0003 (document versioning via metadata, not content overwrite).

git.description: Read access to local git repository: commit history, diffs, branches. Used by agents to understand project evolution without accessing remotes.
git.justification: Agents need git history to understand ADR decisions and feature branches. No push/write needed since branch strategy is local only in this phase.

memory.description: Persistent knowledge graph for project decisions, ubiquitous language (glossary), and domain rules. Survives across agent sessions.
memory.justification: Agents need to read and write domain terms (e.g. 'Gold customer', 'dangerous cargo', 'special freight') and architectural decisions so they are consistent across all generated artifacts.
